coverage_notes: Exhaustive sweep across 7 no-code database platforms (Airtable, NocoDB, Teable, Baserow, Grist, Knack, Smartsheet). Coverage includes official product pages and pricing pages (T0: primary capture of all 7 products), extensive official documentation and API references (T1), comprehensive third-party review aggregators across G2, Capterra, AppSumo (T2), funding records from Crunchbase/PitchBook (T2), analyst reports from Gartner and Forrester on low-code/no-code market (T2), and high-quality practitioner comparisons and teardowns from vendor blogs, professional review sites, and developer communities (T3). Deduplication across ~60+ raw search results yielded 38 unique sources. Verified key URLs via WebFetch. Primary gaps: TrustRadius specific pages (platform exists but reviews not directly URL-captured), some pricing pages redirect or require scroll (captured via search summaries instead). Notable authorities covered: Gartner Magic Quadrant, Forrester Wave, G2 crowd reviews (3220 Airtable reviews, active Baserow/Grist community), Capterra verified reviews, Crunchbase funding (Airtable $1.4B raised, Baserow $5.1M seed, NocoDB $10.5M), analyst reports on market (70%+ enterprise adoption by 2026 projected).

sources.title: Airtable Official Homepage
sources.notes: Official product homepage showcasing Airtable as the leading no-code database platform. Establishes market positioning and primary feature set for ICP-adjacent data frontend.

sources.title: Airtable Pricing Page
sources.notes: Official pricing structure (Free, Team $20/user/mo, Business $45/user/mo, Enterprise custom) with per-seat billing model. Key for competitive pricing analysis.

sources.title: Airtable API Documentation
sources.notes: Official API documentation covering REST endpoints, authentication, rate limits (5 req/sec per base), and integration patterns. Essential for technical capability assessment.

sources.title: Airtable Plans Overview
sources.notes: Official documentation on plan tiers, record limits (1k free, 50k Team, 125k Business, 500k+ Enterprise), storage, and feature availability per tier.

sources.title: Airtable Web API Developer Portal
sources.notes: Developer portal with Web API, Enterprise API, SDKs, and integration guidance. Updated April 17, 2026.

sources.title: Airtable Reviews on G2
sources.notes: 3220 verified user reviews, 4.6/5 stars. Rich HCI evidence: praised for flexibility/ease, criticized for performance lags with large datasets, confusing permissions UX, and non-sharable interfaces.

sources.title: Airtable Reviews on Capterra
sources.notes: 2232 reviews, 4.6/5, 96% positive. Highlights: comprehensive customization, linked records flexibility. Concerns: mobile app weakness, form customization limits, pricing escalation.

sources.title: Airtable Pricing on G2
sources.notes: G2-aggregated pricing data with plan comparison and cost breakdown for competitive benchmarking.

sources.title: Airtable Company Profile & Funding on Crunchbase
sources.notes: Funding record: $1.4B raised across 7 rounds (Series F $735M Dec 2021, Series E $270M); last-round valuation $11.6B (2021); secondary market $4B (Jan 2026). Serves 500k+ orgs, 80% Fortune 100.

sources.title: Airtable on PitchBook
sources.notes: Institutional funding and valuation data for institutional investor perspective on market positioning.

sources.title: Baserow Official Homepage
sources.notes: Open-source no-code database platform positioned as enterprise-grade Airtable alternative. Emphasizes GDPR/HIPAA/SOC2, 150k+ users, cloud + self-hosted options.

sources.title: Baserow Pricing Page
sources.notes: Freemium pricing: Free (unlimited dbs, 3k rows/ws, 2GB), Premium $10/user/mo (50k rows, 20GB), Advanced $18/user/mo, Enterprise custom. Self-hosted free.

sources.title: Baserow GitHub Repository
sources.notes: Open-source repository (MIT license). Source of truth for feature set, architecture (Django+PostgreSQL+Redis), changelog, and community activity. 62k+ GitHub engagement.

sources.title: Baserow REST API Documentation
sources.notes: Official REST API docs with token authentication, auto-generated endpoints per database schema, and integration patterns.

sources.title: Baserow Database API Documentation
sources.notes: User-facing API documentation covering CRUD operations, real-time collaboration, and data management via API.

sources.title: Baserow Changelog
sources.notes: Public changelog tracking feature releases, bug fixes, and product evolution. Recent releases in 2026 visible.

sources.title: Baserow Reviews on G2
sources.notes: Active user reviews praising performance, real-time collaboration, cost efficiency (50-60% cheaper than Airtable). Notes: no native mobile app, limited Kanban on free tier.

sources.title: Baserow Reviews on Capterra
sources.notes: Verified reviews highlighting fast implementation (30min from Airtable), generous free tier, fair pricing. API field names cryptic. Data sovereignty advantage over cloud-only competitors.

sources.title: Baserow on Crunchbase
sources.notes: Funding: $5.1M seed (Jul 2022, updated Sep 2025 round $5.16M from Firstminute/Inkef/Foreword). Founded 2021 by Bram Wiepjes and Olivier Maes.

sources.title: Baserow Review on MakerStack
sources.notes: Expert teardown praising 7.4/10 rating for clear value proposition, open-source trust, and self-hosting freedom. Mobile UX gap noted.

sources.title: NocoDB Cloud Platform
sources.notes: Official NocoDB cloud offering and gateway to documentation. Positions as fastest Airtable alternative with spreadsheet interface over any SQL database.

sources.title: NocoDB GitHub Repository
sources.notes: Open-source (MIT/AGPL), 62k+ GitHub stars (most-starred Airtable clone by wide margin). Architecture: NestJS backend, Nuxt/Vue3 frontend, Pinia state, Ant Design Vue UI. Direct database connector (MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, MSSQL, Oracle, ClickHouse, Snowflake, Databricks).

sources.title: NocoDB Documentation
sources.notes: Official product documentation covering setup, features (sort, filter, group, share), database connections, and API integration. Features Expanded Record Side Panel (2026.05.1).

sources.title: NocoDB Product Documentation Portal
sources.notes: Product documentation with FAQs, feature guides, and community resources. Includes NocoDocs (built-in document editor) and NocoSync integrations.

sources.title: NocoDB API Documentation
sources.notes: Official API reference for programmatic database access and automation.

sources.title: NocoDB (XGenCloud) on Crunchbase
sources.notes: Funding: $10.5M across 2 rounds (seed Oct 2022). 17 investors including Matt Mullenweg, Spencer Kimball. OSS Capital and Decibel Partners lead investors.

sources.title: NocoDB Review on XDA
sources.notes: Hands-on technical review positioning NocoDB as best self-hosted Airtable alternative for teams with existing SQL databases. Data safety considerations flagged.

sources.title: Teable AI Spreadsheet Platform
sources.notes: Official homepage. Positioned as 'AI Spreadsheet for Business' with talk-to-build, batch content generation, self-hosted CE (AGPL). ISO9001/27001 certified.

sources.title: Teable GitHub Repository
sources.notes: Open-source Postgres-powered no-code platform. AGPL Community Edition. Features: Grid, Kanban, Calendar, Gallery, Form views; AI talk-to-build; unlimited rows on free self-hosted.

sources.title: Teable Help Center
sources.notes: Official help documentation covering setup, features, and user guides. Last updated Jan 23, 2026.

sources.title: Teable API Documentation
sources.notes: API reference with authentication (Personal Access Tokens, OAuth), endpoint list, and integration patterns for custom applications.

sources.title: Teable on Crunchbase
sources.notes: Funding record: angel round at seed stage with 3 investors. Limited detail; Teable is newer entrant (2024+).

sources.title: Grist Official Homepage
sources.notes: Official homepage positioning Grist as 'evolution of spreadsheets' combining spreadsheet familiarity with database structure and no-code app builder. Python formulas, relational references, AI assistant, SQLite foundation.

sources.title: Grist Core on GitHub
sources.notes: Open-source Grist core. SQLite-based relational spreadsheet. Public releases page and community engagement visible.

sources.title: Grist Product Features Page
sources.notes: Detailed product features, capabilities, and positioning relative to spreadsheets and databases.

sources.title: Grist REST API Reference
sources.notes: Official REST API for documents, workspaces, team sites. 2026 updates: OAuth credential framework, OIDC server, MCP tools, cellFormat=typed option.

sources.title: Grist Reviews on G2
sources.notes: User reviews highlighting Python support, multi-line formulas, smart auto-columns, row-level access control. Authentication stability and setup barriers noted for non-technical users.

sources.title: Grist Reviews on Capterra
sources.notes: Verified reviews praising Grist as spreadsheet power tool with database structure. HCI evidence: 17-year spreadsheet veteran sees it as ideal platform; small biz customized CRM use case.

sources.title: Grist Reviews on AppSumo
sources.notes: Community reviews: mix of Airtable/GSheets, true alternative, powerful but usability concerns. High row limits (100k+) without premium pricing. No data lock-in (export to CSV, SQLite).

sources.title: Knack No-Code Platform
sources.notes: Official homepage. Positioned as AI-powered no-code app builder generating complete business applications. Knack 2.0 (2026) features AI app generation in 60 seconds.

sources.title: Knack Pricing Page
sources.notes: Official pricing: Starter $19→$49/mo, Pro $49→$110/mo, Corporate $250/mo. Unlimited users (no per-seat). Pricing change October 2026. API access on paid tiers only.

sources.title: Knack Documentation Center
sources.notes: Official documentation covering builder guide, how-to guides (CRM, inventory, class enrollment, quiz apps), API, and support resources.

sources.title: Knack Plans & Pricing Documentation
sources.notes: Official pricing documentation with add-on bundles (records, storage, advanced SSO, flows). Annual discount ~16% savings.

sources.title: Smartsheet Official Homepage
sources.notes: Official homepage positioning Smartsheet as enterprise collaboration and project management platform. Combines spreadsheet and Gantt paradigms with automation, resource management, reporting.

sources.title: Smartsheet Project Management Solutions
sources.notes: Smartsheet's positioning for project management use case. Competes with Airtable in workflow/automation space but enterprise-focused.

sources.title: Smartsheet Developer Portal
sources.notes: Official API and SDK documentation with MCP server support (30+ tools for sheets, rows, columns). Four official SDKs (Python, Java, Node.js, C#).

sources.title: Smartsheet API Introduction
sources.notes: Official API reference covering object schemas, operations, code snippets for sheets, folders, users, and more. Getting started guide with Try It editor.

sources.title: Smartsheet API Changelog
sources.notes: Public changelog tracking API deprecations, new endpoints (sheet paths, reports, dashboards, folders), webhook events, and Claude integration (2026).

sources.title: Gartner Magic Quadrant for Enterprise Low-Code Application Platforms
sources.notes: Gartner 2026 market analysis. Key findings: 70% of new enterprise apps will use low-code/no-code by 2026; 75% by 2026 (revised); 80% by 2029. Citizen developers adoption rising.

sources.title: Forrester Landscape: AppGen and Low-Code Platforms Q2 2026
sources.notes: Forrester 2026 analysis: AppGen platforms automating application creation; 87% of enterprise developers use low-code; 21% sustained annual growth predicted; $50B market by 2028. Emphasizes coordination and integration as differentiators.

sources.title: Research and Markets: No-Code Development Platforms Market Report
sources.notes: Market research: $28.11B (2024) → $35.86B (2025) at 27.6% CAGR. Regional performance: North America 33.90%, Asia Pacific highest growth CAGR. Key players: Microsoft, Salesforce, Mendix, Appian, OutSystems, Pegasystems, ServiceNow, etc.
